extracted.intended_audience: psychoanalytic scholars, students of psychology/literary theory, and researchers of humor
extracted.subtask_description: Theoretical/analytic criteria for understanding how jokes (especially tendentious and obscene ones) are structured, why they provoke laughter, and which psychological/social conditions and technical methods produce them. Focus is on Freudian psychoanalytic interpretation of jokes' function and technique.

rubrics_metrics.name: Woman's inflexibility as condition for smut
rubrics_metrics.description: The woman’s inflexibility is therefore the first condition for the development of smut.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If sexual readiness is not forthcoming and defensive reactions appear, sexually exciting speech is held up and becomes an aim in itself (smut). The presence of another man (a third person) strengthens this condition because immediate surrender by the woman is unlikely; the sexual aggressiveness, blocked from action, becomes hostile and sadistic and derives pleasure from evoking excitement in the woman.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three-person structure of tendentious jokes
rubrics_metrics.description: A tendentious joke calls for three people: the joker, the object of hostile or sexual aggressiveness, and a third in whom the joke’s aim of producing pleasure is fulfilled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is not the person who makes the joke who laughs and enjoys it, but the inactive listener. In smut the same three-person relation operates: the speaker's inhibited libidinal impulse turns hostile against the object and enlists the third person as ally; the listener is bribed by effortless satisfaction of libido.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role of the onlooker/listener (third person)
rubrics_metrics.description: The third person (onlooker/listener) becomes the person to whom smut or tendentious jokes are addressed and who supplies the pleasurable reception.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the direct presence of the woman is absent or ineffective, the onlooker/listener substitutes and receives the obscene utterance. The third person is 'bribed' by the joke into sharing the speaker's aggression or lust without effort, thereby facilitating rebellion or indirect satisfaction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allusion as technique that converts smut into acceptable joke
rubrics_metrics.description: In refined society smut becomes a joke only when it has the character of a joke; the technical method it usually employs is the allusion — replacement by something small, remotely connected, which the hearer reconstructs into a straightforward obscenity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The greater the discrepancy between the explicit form and what the hearer reconstructs, the more refined the joke and the more it can ascend into 'good society'. Allusion and other verbal/conceptual joke methods make obscene content tolerable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jokes circumvent obstacles to instinctual satisfaction
rubrics_metrics.description: Jokes make possible the satisfaction of an instinct (lustful or hostile) in the face of an obstacle that stands in its way by circumventing the obstacle and drawing pleasure from a source made inaccessible by the obstacle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obstacles (e.g., repression or social inhibition) prevent direct satisfaction; jokes allow indirect release and recovery of renounced pleasures by evading censorship through form or disguise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repression and civilization as determinants of tendentious jokes
rubrics_metrics.description: Repression — psychical processes developed by civilization and education — makes direct enjoyment of certain impulses unacceptable, thereby creating conditions in which tendentious jokes retrieve repudiated pleasures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Higher education/social level increases repression; what was formerly agreeable is now rejected. Tendentious jokes provide a means of undoing renunciation and retrieving what was lost; they enable laughter at things one would feel ashamed of if stated plainly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tendentious jokes combine technical and purpose-derived pleasure
rubrics_metrics.description: Tendentious jokes have sources of pleasure besides those open to innocent jokes; part of their appeal arises from their purpose (hostile or sexual aims) as well as from their technique.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because of this mixture, we often cannot distinguish by feeling what portion of the pleasure comes from technique and what from purpose. Consequently, jokes with poor technique may still provoke immense laughter because of their tendentious purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jokes as indirect invective exploiting a third party
rubrics_metrics.description: In hostile jokes the same mechanism arises: inhibited hostile impulses are redirected into joking form so as to enlist the third person and secure enjoyment of overcoming the enemy without direct action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: By making the enemy appear small, despicable or comic through a joke, the speaker secures the listener's alliance (through laughter) and satisfies aggressive tendencies that cannot be expressed directly due to internal or external inhibitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of jokes to attack authority and evade external prohibitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Tendentious jokes are especially favoured for making aggressiveness or criticism possible against persons in exalted positions who claim authority and against institutions protected by external circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because direct disparagement would be risky or forbidden, jokes serve as a form of rebellion and liberation from authority; caricature and joking forms enable criticism that would be unsafe if stated overtly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Façade (comic façade) as concealment for tendentious content
rubrics_metrics.description: Some anecdotes or stories present a comic façade that conceals a forbidden or tendentious meaning; only some people will treat such a façade as a joke (subjective determinant).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The façade can dazzle the examining eye, allowing the joke to conceal not only what it says but also the fact that it has something forbidden to say. This permits the joke to function even when its technique is weak; what one allows oneself to call a joke can be a matter of subjective permission to see through the façade.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cynical jokes attacking institutions (e.g., marriage)
rubrics_metrics.description: A special class of tendentious jokes — cynical jokes — disguise cynicisms and are aimed at institutions, dogmas, and moral or religious views that are strictly guarded but inviting to attack (notably marriage).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cynical jokes often employ bewildering similes, allusion, and omission to insinuate criticism; they declare rebellious truths indirectly (for example, implying marriage fails to satisfy sexual needs) and thereby voice social or moral discontent under cover of humor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sophistical/logical façade and displacement techniques
rubrics_metrics.description: Jokes can use an appearance of logic or sophistry (logical façade) and displacement to present a tolerated point while disguising broader tendentious meaning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An appearance of logic chosen as a compromise can let a thought assert itself partially; sophistical displacement jokes (epicurean examples) say 'yes the man is right' on a single point while avoiding the full unacceptable claim. This technique lets the joke express serious sentiments disguised as clever argument.

rubrics_metrics.name: Displacement and representation by small detail
rubrics_metrics.description: The joke-work often replaces the true target by something small or remote (representation by a small detail), so the hearer reconstructs the larger meaning from the detail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This technique parallels dream-work and allows ridicule or criticism to be conveyed indirectly; examples include using an insignificant trait to stand for something more substantial, enabling laughter at what cannot be openly named.

rubrics_metrics.name: Absurdity and dialect as technical devices
rubrics_metrics.description: Absurdity (apparent illogic) and dialect or narrative skill can function as technical devices to raise laughter or to cloak tendentious content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Absurdity may mask a genuine social critique (making the spoken claim seem illogical while hinting at a deeper truth). Dialect and storytelling competence are often necessary to produce the comic façade and to get the hearer to receive the joke as intended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Marginal cases: stories with little technique but tendentious purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Some stories possess little of joke-technique yet, by virtue of their façade and concealed purpose, produce the full effect of a tendentious joke (they are marginal cases).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such anecdotes can deliver criticism openly or in a thinly disguised way; their poverty of technical methods explains why they sometimes rely on dialect or narrative presentation to secure a laugh.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-criticism as a subjective determinant enabling sharper jokes
rubrics_metrics.description: When the subject (a person or people) participates in the fault being mocked, self-criticism can serve as a subjective determinant that allows jokes to be more direct and revealing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Groups making jokes about their own characteristics (e.g., Jewish popular jokes) can more candidly expose faults because the subject shares in the target, creating permission for sharper tendentious material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jokes can betray serious thoughts (jokes as self-betrayal)
rubrics_metrics.description: Jests often betray something serious: they may covertly state what conscious thought cannot; a joke-work may present as a jest what the thought wishes to assert but cannot do so openly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is analogous to slips of the tongue and other self-betrayal phenomena; a joke's façade can conceal an underlying serious critique, desire, or cynicism that the speaker or culture cannot otherwise admit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Class/education influence on what is laughable
rubrics_metrics.description: Educational and social level influence whether a given obscene or ridiculing element is acceptable; what is laughable at one level will be shameful at another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lower social levels may openly enjoy coarse smut; educated people require refinement (allusion) to laugh at the same content. Thus class shapes both the acceptable form of a joke and its technical refinement.
